title: Hold flats back and catch a memoriser
brief: Write a seeded train/test split and a rule that memorises its training flats, then measure the gap between its training and test risk.
hints: Shuffle positions, not the arrays: order = np.random.default_rng(seed).permutation(n). Then use order[:n_test] and order[n_test:] to index both x and y.
int(0.29 * 100) is 28 because 0.29 * 100 is 28.999999999999996. Add 1e-9 before you convert to int.
memoriser_predict builds a distance table of shape (m, n) with np.abs(x_new[:, None] - x_train[None, :]), takes np.argmin(..., axis=1), and indexes y_train with the result.
generalisation_gap scores the memoriser twice: on the training flats (x_train, y_train) and on the test flats. The gap is test minus train.
